# 2011A Question 13 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Describe**]{.task-verb} the determinants of work of breathing in an adult human at rest.
:::

Also asked in: [2001B Question 2](/content/exams/anzca/2001/B/2/index.qmd#examiner-comments), [2006B Question 10](/content/exams/anzca/2006/B/10/index.qmd#examiner-comments)

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Describe**]{.task-verb} the elastic and resistive components using a labelled pressure–volume graph. Explain surface tension, tissue properties and airflow resistance, then relate their balance to respiratory frequency at rest.

::: {.structure-headings}
### Definition and Pressure–Volume Graph

### Surface Tension and Surfactant

### Elastic Tissue

### Airflow and Tissue Resistance

### Respiratory Frequency
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
This question was passed by **43%** of candidates.

This question was best answered with an accurate labelled and annotated pressure-volume graph. Previous examination reports have detailed the main points expected and these have not changed. There were many poor diagrams that highlighted candidates’ lack of understanding. A common mistake was to describe the determinants of FRC, not those of work of breathing. Discussing how work of breathing changes when not at rest or in disease garnered marks if it helped to explain the underlying concept that was asked for in the question.
:::
